books.why_zh: 「黑暗时代」不黑暗——威克姆以考古与文献的庞大数据推翻'罗马崩溃=文明断裂'的旧叙事，展示后罗马世界如何创造新的政治经济秩序。
books.why_en: The 'Dark Ages' weren't dark — Wickham overturns 'Roman collapse = civilizational break' with massive archaeological/textual data, showing how post-Roman worlds created new political economies.

background.zh: Wickham（牛津大学 Chichele 中世纪史讲座教授 2005–2016、FBA、《Framing the Early Middle Ages》作者）撰写企鹅欧洲史第二卷。核心论题：西罗马帝国 476 年「灭亡」之后，地中海世界并非陷入黑暗，而是在拜占庭、法兰克、伊斯兰、斯拉夫等多条路径上各自演化出新秩序。方法论上强调经济考古（陶器分布、贸易网络）与制度史（税收、地权、教会组织）并重。时间跨度 600 年，地理涵盖从爱尔兰到美索不达米亚、从北欧到北非的整个后罗马世界。获 2010 年 Wolfson History Prize、2014 年 Royal Historical Society Serena Medal。
background.en: By Wickham (Chichele Professor of Medieval History Oxford 2005–2016, FBA 1998; author of Framing the Early Middle Ages). Volume 2, 400–1000. Core thesis: after the 'fall' of 476, the Mediterranean world did not enter darkness but evolved new orders along Byzantine, Frankish, Islamic, and Slavic paths. Methodologically combines economic archaeology (pottery distribution, trade networks) with institutional history (taxation, land, church organization). Spans 600 years and the entire post-Roman world from Ireland to Mesopotamia. Winner of the 2010 Wolfson History Prize; RHS Serena Medal 2014 for related work.

plot_acts.zh: 400–1000｜「黑暗时代」的破除——为什么 400–1000 的欧洲不能用「罗马灭亡 = 黑暗」一笔抹掉。
plot_acts.en: 400–1000｜Dismantling the 'Dark Ages': why 400–1000 cannot be dismissed as post-Roman darkness.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 导论把『Inheritance』一词从制度史范畴解放出来 —— 罗马之后 600 年，欧洲任何政权都不得不引用罗马作为合法性来源；这本书要写的是这种『引用』的物质基础。
plot_acts.arg_en: Introduction liberates 'inheritance' from institutional history — for 600 years after Rome every regime cited Roman legitimacy; the book is about the material base of that citation.

brief.main: 导论 —— 『Inheritance』不是制度史范畴，而是合法性来源。任何 400-1000 的政权 (法兰克、西哥特、东哥特、汪达尔、伦巴德、拜占庭、倭马亚、加洛林、奥托) 都不得不引用罗马。第一部分的六章 (Ch.2-7) 处理 400-700 的地中海世界。
brief.flow: Ch.2 罗马帝国的行政-财政默认设定 → Ch.3 五世纪西部的分裂 (西哥特 418、汪达尔 439、东哥特 493、法兰克 481、勃艮第 443) → Ch.4 不列颠与爱尔兰的边缘化 → Ch.5 东地中海 (拜占庭) 的正统延续 → Ch.6 斯拉夫-阿瓦尔-保加尔的多瑙河移民 → Ch.7 六世纪地中海贸易网的最后完整形态。
brief.names: Honorius、Arcadius、Theodosius II、Valentinian III、Attila、Odoacer、Theodoric、Clovis、Amalasuntha、Belisarius、Justinian、Heraclius；地名 Ravenna、Constantinople、Carthage、Alexandria、Antioch
brief.sources: Chronicle of Marcellinus Comes、Cassiodorus《-variarum》、Procopius《战史》《秘史》、Gregory of Tours《法兰克人史》、Isidore of Seville《编年史》、Bishop 墓葬铭文、非洲-东方红彩陶 ARS 分布图
brief.link: 第一部分建立全书的『地中海中心』视角 —— 反对任何把法兰克-加洛林当作 400-1000 主轴的传统。
brief.main_en: Introduction — 'Inheritance' is not a category of institutional history but of the sources of legitimacy. Every regime from 400 to 1000 (Frankish, Visigothic, Ostrogothic, Vandal, Lombard, Byzantine, Umayyad, Carolingian, Ottonian) had to invoke Rome. The six chapters of Part One (ch. 2-7) treat the Mediterranean world of 400-700.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 2 the administrative-fiscal default of the Roman Empire → ch. 3 the fifth-century fragmentation of the West (Visigoths 418, Vandals 439, Ostrogoths 493, Franks 481, Burgundians 443) → ch. 4 the marginalisation of Britain and Ireland → ch. 5 the orthodox continuity of the eastern Mediterranean (Byzantium) → ch. 6 the Slavic-Avar-Bulgar migration on the Danube → ch. 7 the last complete form of the sixth-century Mediterranean trade web.
brief.names_en: Honorius, Arcadius, Theodosius II, Valentinian III, Attila, Odoacer, Theodoric, Clovis, Amalasuntha, Belisarius, Justinian, Heraclius; the places Ravenna, Constantinople, Carthage, Alexandria, Antioch
brief.sources_en: Chronicle of Marcellinus Comes, Cassiodorus's Variae, Procopius's Wars and Secret History, Gregory of Tours's History of the Franks, Isidore of Seville's Chronica, bishops' funerary inscriptions, maps of African red-slip (ARS) distribution
brief.link_en: Part One establishes the book's 'Mediterranean-centred' perspective — against any tradition that treats the Frankish-Carolingian world as the main axis of 400-1000.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第一部分 · 罗马帝国及其崩解
plot_acts.title_en: PART I · The Roman Empire and its Break-up
plot_acts.zh: 400–550｜帝国的重量（第 2-4 章）：税制、文化信仰、400-550 危机与延续——东地中海仍是 Roman world。
plot_acts.en: 400–550｜The Weight of Empire (chs.2-4): taxation, Christian culture, crisis and continuity — the East remains Roman.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第一部分 (Ch.2-7) —— 地中海世界 400-700。Wickham 的核心论证：东地中海 (拜占庭) 才是延续罗马财政-城市的正统，西部 (法兰克、西哥特) 反而是变体。这一颠倒贯穿全书。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part I (Chs.2-7) Mediterranean 400-700 — Byzantium, not the Frankish and Visigothic West, is the true inheritor of Roman fiscal-urban tradition. This inversion structures the whole book.

brief.main: 第二部分 —— 拜占庭与伊斯兰作为两个『东方』的对称史。作者明确反对把拜占庭处理为『衰落中的罗马余烬』，也反对把早期伊斯兰处理为『沙漠征服』—— 两者都是 600-900 地中海东岸真正的罗马-波斯遗产继承者。
brief.flow: Ch.12 拜占庭 610-1025 (希拉克略的希腊化、圣像破坏、马其顿复兴) → Ch.13 伊斯兰的起源与倭马亚 (622-750) → Ch.14 阿拔斯 (750-945) 与巴格达 → Ch.15 两者的接触带 (奇里乞亚、塞浦路斯、克里特、西西里、伊比利亚) → Ch.16 拜占庭的行政-军区 (theme) 制度 → Ch.17 倭马亚-阿拔斯的税制 (kharaj、jizya) 与罗马-萨珊遗产的接续。
brief.names: Heraclius、Constans II、Leo III、Constantine V、Irene、Nikephoros I、Basil I、Leo VI、Romanos I、Nikephoros II Phokas、John I Tzimiskes、Basil II；Muhammad、Abu Bakr、Umar、Uthman、Ali、Muawiya、Abd al-Malik、al-Walid、Harun al-Rashid、al-Mamun
brief.sources: Theophanes《Chronographia》、Nikephoros《Breviary》、al-Tabari《史册》、al-Baladhuri《征服之书》、伊德里斯诸地图、罗马-波斯边界考古、死海纸莎草、阿拉伯税册 (P.Yadin、CPAI)
brief.link: 把拜占庭与伊斯兰处理为对称的两个『东方』—— 为第三部分加洛林出场做对比铺垫。
brief.main_en: Part Two — a symmetrical history of Byzantium and Islam as two 'Easts'. The author explicitly rejects treating Byzantium as a 'decaying ember of Rome' or early Islam as a 'desert conquest': both are true inheritors of the Roman-Persian legacy on the eastern Mediterranean from 600 to 900.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 12 Byzantium 610-1025 (Heraclius's Hellenisation, Iconoclasm, the Macedonian renaissance) → ch. 13 the origins of Islam and the Umayyads (622-750) → ch. 14 the Abbasids (750-945) and Baghdad → ch. 15 their contact zone (Cilicia, Cyprus, Crete, Sicily, Iberia) → ch. 16 Byzantine administration and the theme system → ch. 17 Umayyad-Abbasid taxation (kharaj, jizya) and the continuation of the Roman-Sasanian legacy.
brief.names_en: Heraclius, Constans II, Leo III, Constantine V, Irene, Nikephoros I, Basil I, Leo VI, Romanos I, Nikephoros II Phokas, John I Tzimiskes, Basil II; Muhammad, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Muawiya, Abd al-Malik, al-Walid, Harun al-Rashid, al-Mamun
brief.sources_en: Theophanes's Chronographia, Nikephoros's Breviary, al-Tabari's History, al-Baladhuri's Book of Conquests, the maps of al-Idrisi, Roman-Persian frontier archaeology, the Dead Sea papyri, Arab tax registers (P. Yadin, CPAI)
brief.link_en: Treats Byzantium and Islam as two symmetrical 'Easts' — setting up a contrast for the Carolingian entrance in Part Three.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第二部分 · 后罗马西方
plot_acts.zh: 550–750｜墨洛兰高卢、西地中海王国（西/意）、无国家的英爱、后罗马心态、财富与农民、物质展示的权力（第 5-10 章）。
plot_acts.en: 550–750｜Merovingian Gaul, Spanish/Italian kingdoms, stateless Britain/Ireland, mentality, economy, material display (chs.5-10).
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第二部分 (Ch.8-14) —— 三个世界 (拜占庭 / 倭马亚-阿拔斯 / 加洛林) 的对称史。作者拒绝『西方 vs 东方』的单向叙事 —— 八世纪地中海是三个政体的竞争场。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part II (Chs.8-14) — symmetrical history of three worlds: Byzantium, Umayyad-Abbasid, Carolingian. Rejects one-way West-vs-East; 8th-c. Mediterranean is a three-power arena.

brief.main: 第三部分 —— 西部 400-800 的成形。作者拒绝把 476 作为分界，把 500-750 处理为一个缓慢的『从地中海帝国到北海王国』的转位过程 —— 墨洛温、威尼斯-拉文纳总督区、爱尔兰-苏格兰修道网、威塞克斯七王国并行演化。
brief.flow: Ch.8 墨洛温高卢-勃艮第-奥斯特拉西亚 (481-751) → Ch.9 财富交换 —— 全书经济学心脏，处理货币、税制、贸易路线 → Ch.10 不列颠从罗马到七王国 (500-800) → Ch.11 爱尔兰与苏格兰的修道岛 → Ch.12 伊比利亚的西哥特王国 (589 Recaredo 皈依天主教 - 711 伊斯兰征服) → Ch.13 亚平丁半岛与教皇国的形成 → Ch.14 弗里斯兰-萨克森-法兰克的北海沿岸。
brief.names: Clovis、Dagobert I、Grifo、Pepin of Herstal、Charles Martel、Pepin III、Gregory of Tours、Columban、Columba、Brendan、Aidan、Wilfrid、Beda、Reccared、Tariq ibn Ziyad、Liutprand、Ratchis、Aistulf、Zachary、Stephen II
brief.sources: Gregory of Tours《法兰克人史》《图尔主教传》、Liber Historiae Francorum、Beda《英吉利教会史》、Codex Aurora、Lex Salica、Lex Visigothorum (Liber Iudiciorum)、都尔-图尔会议决议、Freedgar _continuatio_、Bautas 银器、Sutton Hoo 船葬、Clonmacnoise、Iona、Durrow 福音书、Lindisfarne 福音书
brief.link: Ch.9 财富交换部分是全书经济学核心 —— 后续的政制-文化讨论都是这层的次生现象。
brief.main_en: Part Three — the forming of the post-Roman West, 400-800. The author refuses 476 as a dividing line, treating 500-750 as a slow displacement 'from a Mediterranean empire to North Sea kingdoms' — Merovingian, the Venetian-Ravennan exarchate, the Irish-Scottish monastic web and the West Saxon Heptarchy evolving in parallel.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 8 Merovingian Gaul-Burgundy-Austrasia (481-751) → ch. 9 the exchange of wealth, the economic heart of the book, treating coinage, taxation and trade routes → ch. 10 Britain from Rome to the Heptarchy (500-800) → ch. 11 the monastic isles of Ireland and Scotland → ch. 12 the Visigothic kingdom in Iberia (Reccared's conversion to Catholicism 589 to the Islamic conquest 711) → ch. 13 the Italian peninsula and the forming of the Papal States → ch. 14 the Frisian-Saxon-Frankish North Sea coast.
brief.names_en: Clovis, Dagobert I, Grifo, Pepin of Herstal, Charles Martel, Pepin III, Gregory of Tours, Columban, Columba, Brendan, Aidan, Wilfrid, Bede, Reccared, Tariq ibn Ziyad, Liutprand, Ratchis, Aistulf, Zachary, Stephen II
brief.sources_en: Gregory of Tours's History of the Franks and Life of the Bishops of Tours, Liber Historiae Francorum, Bede's Ecclesiastical History, Codex Aureus, Lex Salica, Lex Visigothorum (Liber Iudiciorum), the councils of Tours, the Continuation of Fredegar, the Bautes silver, the Sutton Hoo ship-burial, Clonmacnoise, Iona, the Book of Durrow, the Lindisfarne Gospels
brief.link_en: The 'exchange of wealth' chapter is the book's economic core — all later political and cultural discussion is a secondary phenomenon of this layer.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第三部分 · 东方的诸帝国
plot_acts.title_en: PART III · The Empires of the East
plot_acts.zh: 550–1000｜拜占庭的存续与复兴、阿拉伯政治权力的凝结（630-750）、从阿拔斯巴格达到倭马亚科尔多瓦、东地中海交换（第 11-15 章）。
plot_acts.en: 550–1000｜Byzantine survival/revival, Arab state-making, Abbasid-to-Umayyad axis, eastern Mediterranean exchange (chs.11-15).
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第三部分 (Ch.15-20) —— 加洛林之后 850-1000 的分裂。第二次封建化、维京-马扎尔-萨拉森三边压力、 Ottonian 复兴 —— 现代欧洲的地理-政治雏形在这一段定型。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part III (Chs.15-20) post-Carolingian fragmentation 850-1000. Second feudalisation, Viking-Magyar-Saracen pressure, Ottonian revival — Europe's modern geo-political shape crystallises here.

brief.main: 第四部分 —— 加洛林 (750-900) 与其解体后的第二次封建化 (900-1000)。这是本书的顶点 —— 查理曼与奥托、阿尔昆与艾因哈德、维京与马扎尔、《凡尔登条约》与《梅尔森条约》、修道院改革与庄园经济。现代欧洲的地理-政治雏形在这一段定型。
brief.flow: Ch.15 查理曼与加洛林文艺复兴 (768-814) → Ch.16 路易一世的内乱与凡尔登 (843) → Ch.17 秃头查理、日耳曼人路易、查理三世与加洛林解体 → Ch.18 维京、马扎尔、萨拉森三边压力 (860-955) → Ch.19 奥托复兴与神圣罗马帝国 (919-1024) → Ch.20 卡佩王朝的西法兰克 (987-1031) 与英格兰威塞克斯 → Ch.21 从 900 到 1000 的『欧洲的窄门』—— 人口、农业、聚落形态 → Ch.22 农奴化 —— 全书最原创的收尾论题。
brief.names: Charles Martel、Pepin III、Charlemagne、Louis the Pious、Lothar I、Charles the Bald、Louis the German、Lothar II、Charles the Fat、Arnulf、Louis the Blind、Hugh Capet、Robert II、Otto I、Otto II、Otto III、Henry II、Alcuin、Einhard、Rabanus Maurus、John Scotus Eriugena、Odo of Cluny、Bruno of Querfurt、Adalbero of Reims、Gerbert of Aurillac
brief.sources: Royal Frankish Annals、Nithard《Histories》、Umberto《Chronicon》、Widukind《Saxon deeds》、Thietmar of Merseburg《Chronicle》、Annales Bertiniani/Fuldenses、Polyptyque of Irminon、Polyptyque of St-Germain-des-Prés、Capitularia Regum Francorum、Cluny charters、Corbie/Prüm/Fulda 隐修院档案、Stellenbau 与 Three-field system 考古
brief.link: Ch.22 农奴化是全书最原创的收尾论题 —— 用文献 (capitularies、polyptyques) 与考古 (村庄形态变化) 双证。
brief.main_en: Part Four — the Carolingians (750-900) and the second feudalisation after their dissolution (900-1000). This is the book's summit: Charlemagne and Otto, Alcuin and Einhard, Vikings and Magyars, the treaties of Verdun and Mersen, monastic reform and the manor economy. The geographic-political template of modern Europe takes shape here.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 15 Charlemagne and the Carolingian renaissance (768-814) → ch. 16 Louis the Pious's civil wars and Verdun (843) → ch. 17 Charles the Bald, Louis the German, Charles III and the Carolingian dissolution → ch. 18 the three-way pressure of Vikings, Magyars and Saracens (860-955) → ch. 19 the Ottonian renewal and the Holy Roman Empire (919-1024) → ch. 20 the Capetian West Frankish kingdom (987-1031) and Wessex in England → ch. 21 the 'narrow gate of Europe' from 900 to 1000 — population, agriculture, settlement form → ch. 22 enserfment, the book's most original closing thesis.
brief.names_en: Charles Martel, Pepin III, Charlemagne, Louis the Pious, Lothar I, Charles the Bald, Louis the German, Lothar II, Charles the Fat, Arnulf, Louis the Blind, Hugh Capet, Robert II, Otto I, Otto II, Otto III, Henry II, Alcuin, Einhard, Rabanus Maurus, John Scotus Eriugena, Odo of Cluny, Bruno of Querfurt, Adalbero of Reims, Gerbert of Aurillac
brief.sources_en: Royal Frankish Annals, Nithard's Histories, Widukind's De Rebus Saxonis, Thietmar of Merseburg's Chronicle, the Annals of St-Bertin and of Fulda, the Polyptych of Irminon, the Polyptych of St-Germain-des-Prés, the Capitularia Regum Francorum, the Cluny charters, the archives of Corbie/Prüm/Fulda, archaeology of the holloway-village (Stellenbau) and three-field system
brief.link_en: The enserfment chapter is the book's most original closing thesis — argued on a double basis of texts (capitularies, polyptychs) and archaeology (changes in village form).

plot_acts.title_zh: 第四部分 · 加洛林与后加洛林西方
plot_acts.title_en: PART IV · The Carolingian and Post-Carolingian West
plot_acts.zh: 750–1000｜加洛林世纪、知识分子与政治、10 世纪继承国、加洛林式英格兰、外围欧洲、贵族与农奴化（第 16-22 章）。
plot_acts.en: 750–1000｜Carolingian century, intellectuals, tenth-century successors, Carolingian England, outer Europe, aristocrats and peasant enclosure (chs.16-22).
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第四部分 (Ch.21-22) —— 从公元 900 到 1000 的『欧洲的窄门』。作者用人口、农业、定居形态的变化，说明 1000 之后的一切盛期中世纪成就都是这窄门的果。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part IV (Chs.21-22) — Europe's narrow door 900-1000. Population, agriculture, settlement forms show that everything High Medieval owes to this bottleneck.

brief.main: 第五部分 —— 600 年结构性趋势的总结。Wickham 把 400-1000 的政治、经济、社会、宗教、文化五条线并列陈述 —— 每条都在 400-700、700-900、900-1000 三段中各自演化。全书的宏观论旨在这一段陈述。
brief.flow: Ch.23 政治形态的多样性 (罗马遗产 / 王国 / 帝国 / 城邦 / 部落) → Ch.24 经济 (税制 / 贸易 / 货币 / 农业) 的三段演化 → Ch.25 社会结构 (贵族 / 农民 / 奴隶 / 自由人 / 边缘群体) 的重组 → Ch.26 宗教 (基督教、伊斯兰、犹太、斯拉夫多神) 的传播与冲突 → Ch.27 文化 (拉丁、希腊、阿拉伯、方言) 的多中心 → Ch.28 女性与家庭在制度与经济中的位置 → Ch.29 结语 —— 欧洲的窄门通向 1000 之后的盛期中世纪。
brief.names: 跨段落的历史人物密集出现，本节以结构性人物为主 —— 修士、主教、郡伯、可萨汗、斯拉夫公爵、维京 jarl、穆斯林卡迪
brief.sources: 全书 600 年一手材料总汇 —— 编年史、铭文、纸莎草、陶器、聚落、墓地、税册、会议决议、修道院档案
brief.link: 第 V 部分不是新的实证章节，而是把 Ch.2-Ch.22 的具体材料抽象成趋势论。
brief.main_en: Part Five — a synthesis of six centuries of structural trend. Wickham sets out the political, economic, social, religious and cultural lines of 400-1000 side by side, each evolving across the three phases 400-700, 700-900 and 900-1000. The book's macro-theses are stated in this section.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 23 the diversity of political forms (Roman inheritance / kingdoms / empire / city-states / tribes) → ch. 24 the three-phase evolution of the economy (taxation / trade / coinage / agriculture) → ch. 25 the reordering of social structure (nobles / peasants / slaves / freemen / marginal groups) → ch. 26 the spread and conflict of the religions (Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Slavic polytheism) → ch. 27 the polycentric culture (Latin, Greek, Arabic, vernacular) → ch. 28 women and the family in institution and economy → ch. 29 conclusion — the narrow gate of Europe opening into the high Middle Ages after 1000.
brief.names_en: Historical figures appear densely across the period; this section features structural figures — monks, bishops, counts, Khazar khagans, Slavic dukes, Viking jarls, Muslim qadis
brief.sources_en: A synthesis of six centuries of first-hand material across the whole book — chronicles, inscriptions, papyri, pottery, settlements, cemeteries, tax registers, council acts, monastic archives
brief.link_en: Part Five is not a new evidentiary chapter but an abstraction of the specific material of ch. 2-22 into a theory of trends.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第二十三章 · 结语：400-1000 欧洲历史的趋势
plot_acts.title_en: Chapter 23 · Conclusion: Trends in European History, 400–1000
plot_acts.zh: 400–1000｜从地中海到北海，从多神教到一神教——一个千年里欧洲的物质、政治与文化重心如何偏移。
plot_acts.en: 400–1000｜Mediterranean-to-North-Sea, poly- to mono-theism: how Europe's material, political and cultural centre of gravity shifted over 600 years.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 结语把 400-1000 六百年收束为一个统一过程 —— 从地中海中心到北海-莱茵-易北中心的缓慢北移 + 农民自由的逐步丧失 (enclosure of the peasantry)。全书的宏观论旨。
plot_acts.arg_en: Conclusion: six centuries as one process — slow north-shift from Mediterranean to North Sea / Rhine / Elbe + progressive loss of peasant freedom (enclosure). The book's macro-thesis.

brief.main: 结语 —— 400-1000 六百年是一个统一过程。两个宏观论旨：(1) 欧洲重心从地中海缓慢北移到北海-莱茵-易北轴；(2) 农民自由在 700-1000 被一步步关进庄园 (enclosure of the peasantry)。两者共同解释了 1000 之后盛期中世纪的所有条件。
brief.flow: 重心理论 (Pirenne thesis 的修正版 —— 不是伊斯兰逼走地中海，而是北方开发) → 农奴化进程 (从 capitularies 与 polyptyques 追踪) → 与同期其他中世纪通史 (Collins、Fouracre、Noble、Wickham 自己的 Framing) 的比较 → 1000 年前夜的欧洲作为『窄门』的开放收束。
brief.names: Pirenne、Seebohm、Dopsch、Halsall、Wickham 自己 (作为学术自传)
brief.sources: 结语不引新档案，而是回扣前二十二章的一手证据链 —— 以陶器、税册与编年史的跨区域比对，收束「罗马性如何在地方被续用与改造」这一贯穿全书的总问题。
brief.link: 与 Vol.3 (Jordan 盛期中世纪) 直接衔接 —— Wickham 的结语正是 Jordan 的序章。
brief.main_en: Conclusion — the six centuries 400-1000 form a single process. Two macro-theses: (1) Europe's centre of gravity shifts slowly north, from the Mediterranean to the North Sea-Rhine-Elbe axis; (2) peasant freedom is step by step enclosed into the manor between 700 and 1000. Together they explain every condition of the high Middle Ages after 1000.
brief.flow_en: The thesis of the northern shift (a revised Pirenne thesis — not Islam forcing out the Mediterranean, but the opening up of the North) → the process of enserfment (tracked from capitularies and polyptychs) → comparison with other medieval syntheses of the period (Collins, Fouracre, Noble, Wickham's own Framing the Early Middle Ages) → Europe on the eve of the year 1000 as a 'narrow gate', an open-ended close.
brief.names_en: Pirenne, Seebohm, Dopsch, Halsall, Wickham himself (as intellectual autobiography)
brief.sources_en: The conclusion cites no new archives but recalls the first-hand chain of evidence of the preceding twenty-two chapters, closing on the book's through-question — how Romanness was locally continued and transformed — by cross-regional comparison of pottery, tax registers and chronicles.
brief.link_en: Connects directly to Vol. 3 (Jordan, the high Middle Ages) — Wickham's conclusion is precisely Jordan's preface.

narrative.zh: 大空间比较结构：按政治体分区（拜占庭、西欧拉丁、伊斯兰、北方斯拉夫/维京）而非单纯编年；每区内再按时间展开。经济考古证据先行——从陶器、钱币、沉船重建贸易网络地图，然后叠加制度分析。
narrative.en: Large-space comparative structure: organized by polity (Byzantine, Latin West, Islamic, Northern Slavic/Viking) rather than pure chronology; within each, temporal progression. Economic-archaeological evidence leads — trade networks rebuilt from pottery, coins, shipwrecks, then institutional analysis layered on.

plot_flow.zh: 查士丁尼与6世纪地中海

characters.name: Charlemagne · 查理曼
characters.role_zh: 742–814，800 年圣诞加冕——本书第四部分的核心
characters.role_en: Carolingian Empire — 742–814, crowned at Christmas 800; the core of the book's Part Four

characters.name: Muhammad · 穆罕默德
characters.role_zh: 570–632，伊斯兰建国——第三部分东地中海新秩序的起点
characters.role_en: Arab-Islamic — 570–632, the founding of Islam; the start of the eastern Mediterranean's new order in Part Three

characters.name: Gregory the Great · 大格里高利
characters.role_zh: 540–604，教皇君主制的雏形与向英格兰的宣教
characters.role_en: Papacy of Rome — 540–604, the embryo of papal monarchy and the mission to England

characters.name: Basil II · 巴西尔二世
characters.role_zh: 958–1025，拜占庭复兴的顶点——第三部分的关键人物
characters.role_en: Byzantium — 958–1025, the apex of the Byzantine revival; a key figure of Part Three

characters.name: Alcuin of York · 约克的阿尔昆
characters.role_zh: 735–804，卡洛林文艺复兴的教育总设计师
characters.role_en: Carolingian learning — 735–804, the chief designer of the Carolingian Renaissance's education

quotes.orig: And, as will be stressed often in this book, a common language had very little to do with any form of cultural or political solidarity at all.
quotes.trans_zh: 正如本书将反复强调的：共同的语言，与文化或政治上的团结几乎全无必然关系。
quotes.source: Wickham《罗马的遗产：黑暗时代 400–1000》· 导论 · Introduction

intent.reception_good_zh: 「自Pirenne《中世纪的城市》以来最有力的地中海经济史综合」；数据密度惊人但论证清晰。
intent.reception_good_en: 'The most powerful Mediterranean economic synthesis since Pirenne'; staggering data density with clear argumentation.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 主要保留有三：不列颠与爱尔兰在「欧洲」叙事里被显著淡化，重心始终在地中海与法兰克核心地带；经济论证高度依赖考古数据（陶器分布、贸易网络），部分学者质疑其从物证到生产关系的推断跳跃过大；至于以「照亮黑暗时代」为副题，作者虽在正文中解构这一标签，封面却仍倚仗其传播力，而中世纪学界对本是否应复活该词本就分歧。
intent.reception_bad_en: Three main reservations: Britain and Ireland are markedly down-weighted in the 'Europe' narrative, with the focus held on the Mediterranean and the Frankish heartland; the economic argument leans heavily on archaeological data (pottery distributions, trade webs), and some scholars read a too-quick inference from material evidence to relations of production; and while the subtitle 'Illuminating the Dark Ages' deconstructs the loaded label in the text, the cover still trades on its market pull, which medievalists dispute reviving at all.
intent.syn_zh: 「黑暗时代」是一个神话——Wickham 以此卷为欧洲最常被忽视的六百年正名。
intent.syn_en: 'Dark Ages' is a myth — Wickham's volume rehabilitates Europe's most neglected six centuries.

craft.en: Integrating economic archaeology (pottery, coins, shipwrecks) as institutional-historical evidence

craft.en: Dissolves West/Byzantium/Islam triad through comparative economic history.

craft.zh: 章节极长 (30-40 页) —— 每章自成一篇专题论文；建议主题阅读而非通读。

motifs.evid_en: Pottery, trade routes, tax systems — after Rome, material life still takes Rome as its reference.

motifs.evid_en: Byzantium, the Franks, the Umayyads, the Abbasids — 'inheriting Rome' is not a single line but many poles.

motifs.evid_zh: 六百年里欧洲的重心缓慢北移，本书的地理学主轴。
motifs.evid_en: Over six centuries Europe's centre of gravity drifts slowly north — the book's geographic main axis.

motifs.evid_zh: 第 22 章的核心论点——加洛林之后农民的自由被一步步关进庄园。
motifs.evid_en: The core thesis of ch. 22 — after the Carolingians, peasant freedom is enclosed step by step into the manor.

excerpts.orig: This is an extract from a Greek-Latin primer for children, probably of the early fourth century. It expresses, through its very simplicity, some of the unquestioned assumptions of the late Roman empire. Judicial violence was normal, indeed deserved (in fact, even witnesses were routinely tortured unless they were from the élite); and the rich got off. The Roman world was habituated to violence and injustice. The gladiatorial shows of the early empire continued in the fourth-century western empire, despite being banned by Constantine in 326 under Christian influence. In the 380s Alypius, a future ascetic bishop in Africa, went to the games in Rome, brought by friends against his will; he kept his eyes shut, but the roar of the crowd as a gladiator was wounded made him open his eyes and then he was gripped by the blood, ‘just one of the crowd’, as his friend the great theologian Augustine of Hippo (d. 430) sympathetically put it. Augustine, an uncompromising but also not a naive man, took it for granted that such a blood lust was, however sinful in Christian eyes, normal. Actually, all the post-Roman societies, pagan, Christian or Muslim, were equally used to violence, particularly by the powerful; but under the Roman empire it had a public legitimacy, an element of weekly spectacle, which surpassed even the culture of public execution in eighteenth-century Europe. There was a visceral element to Roman power; even after gladiatorial shows ended in the early fifth century, the killing of wild beasts in public continued for another hundred years and more.
excerpts.trans_zh: 罗马帝国不是一个短暂的征服事件，而是一种持续数百年的政治-文化重量。

excerpts.note_en: 'The Weight of Empire' — Roman taxation, law and diocesan map kept shaping the post-Roman West.

read_through.verdict_zh: Wickham 29 章的实质是一部『没有黑暗时代』的物质史——他把 400-1000 六百年拆成东-西-南三轴并行的连续变化，反对任何单一起点（476/800/911）。通读之后最能立住的论断有两条：(1) 罗马之后欧洲的『重心理事北移』是缓慢过程，不是查理曼的人为转向；(2) 从 700 到 1000 三百年里，欧洲农民的自由被一步步关进庄园——农奴化是本书最原创的收尾。全书对『拜占庭-伊斯兰-加洛林』的对称处理，是让 400-1000 真正可读的唯一方法。
read_through.verdict_en: Wickham's 29 chapters are a material history without any 'Dark Ages' — six centuries decomposed into East-West-South parallel continuities, refusing all single starting-points (476/800/911). Two theses hold best on a full read: (1) the north-shift of Europe's gravity is a slow process, not Charlemagne's decision; (2) peasant freedom is enclosed into the manor over 700-1000 — the enclosure of the peasantry is the book's most original closing argument. His symmetrical treatment of Byzantium/Islam/Carolingian is the only method that makes 400-1000 readable.

observations.title_zh: 「帝国的重量」的实际用法
observations.title_en: How 'the weight of empire' actually operates
observations.note_zh: 第 1 部分标题看似修辞，实际是本书的方法论声明——Wickham 反复主张罗马之后 300 年，税制、法律、主教辖区、道路、城市仍构成任何新政权的『默认设定』；这个论断在 Ch.2、Ch.7、Ch.15、Ch.22 都被实证回归，是全书最强的连续论证线。
observations.note_en: 'Weight of empire' is the book's methodological claim: for 300 years post-Rome, taxation, law, dioceses, roads, and cities remained every successor regime's default setting — Chs. 2/7/15/22 keep returning to it empirically; the strongest continuous thread.

observations.title_zh: 第 9 章（财富交换）被低估
observations.note_zh: 全书的经济学心脏其实在 Ch.9 —— 陶器-贸易-税制三角 —— 后续章节的政制与文化讨论都是这层的次生现象；如果只精读三章，我推荐 Ch.1、Ch.9、Ch.22。
observations.note_en: The economic heart is Ch.9 (pottery-trade-tax triangle) — the political and cultural chapters are second-order. If reading only three: Chs. 1, 9, 22.

observations.title_zh: 第 22 章『农奴化』的方法论意义
observations.note_zh: 结尾部分把 700-1000 的农民自由损失作为核心论题 —— 用文献（capitularies、polyptyques）与考古（村庄形态变化）双证。这条线在中文世界讨论中世纪早期时几乎未被引介，值得单独作为专题重读。
observations.note_en: Ends with peasant enclosure 700-1000 as the core thesis — capitularies + village archaeology. Under-cited in Chinese medieval scholarship; worth a thematic re-read.

observations.title_zh: 「多个继承者」vs 「一个西方」
observations.note_zh: Wickham 反复强调拜占庭、倭马亚、阿拔斯、加洛林都在『继承罗马』；这个多极视角在 Ch.12 (Byzantium)、Ch.13 (Islam)、Ch.15 (Carolingian) 平行展开——是全书对『西方文明起源』叙事的最有力批评。
observations.note_en: Byzantium, Umayyad, Abbasid, Carolingian all inheriting Rome — Chs. 12/13/15 develop this symmetrically; the strongest counter-narrative to 'the West'.

full_analysis.zh: **通读后的整体判断**：Wickham 本书是他 2005 年 1200 页学术专著《Framing the Early Middle Ages》的通史版改写 —— 但内容不是简化，是重构。全书最独特之处是把 400-1000 处理为**同时**发生的东地中海史、西亚史、西北欧史，任何一处单极叙事都会破坏这个对称。第二条主线：物质连续性的证据密度 —— 陶器、贸易路线、税册、修道院田产登记 (polyptyques)、聚落形态 —— Wickham 让制度史从考古数据里生长出来，这是本书与任何同期中世纪通史 (如 Collins、Fouracre、Noble) 最根本的区别。局限：(1) 军事史与外交史几乎完全被抽象化 —— 732 Poitiers、843 Verdun、955 Lechfeld 这些事件只在结构讨论里被引用；(2) 对不列颠-爱尔兰-斯堪的纳维亚的处理相对薄弱，重心明显在地中海；(3) 女性与家庭的处理仅限于第 19 章的一节，与 Wickham 自己在《Framing》中已有的性别讨论相比反而收缩。
full_analysis.en: **Overall verdict after a full read**: Wickham's book is a survey-scale reconstruction (not simplification) of his 1,200-page academic Framing the Early Middle Ages (2005). The distinctive move is treating 400-1000 as simultaneously Eastern Mediterranean, West Asian, and North-West European history — any single-pole narrative breaks the symmetry. Second thread: material continuity evidence density (pottery, trade, taxation, monastery polyptyques, settlement form) lets institutional history grow from archaeology, which is the fundamental difference from contemporaries (Collins, Fouracre, Noble). Limitations: (1) military and diplomatic history is largely abstracted — 732, 843, 955 appear only within structural discussion; (2) Britain-Ireland-Scandinavia treatment is comparatively thin, weight is Mediterranean; (3) women and family limited to a single sub-section in Ch.19, a contraction relative to Framing's own gender discussion.

books.why_zh: 欧洲「起飞」的三百年——从千年将至的恐惧到十字军、大学、大教堂、议会——Jordan 是英语世界最好的中世纪通识写手。
books.why_en: Europe's three-century takeoff — from millennium fears to crusades, universities, cathedrals, parliaments — Jordan is the English-speaking world's finest medieval generalist.

background.zh: Jordan（普林斯顿大学中世纪史教授，以法国卡佩王朝研究闻名）撰写第三卷，时间跨度约1000–1300。核心论题：11–13世纪欧洲的「全面扩张」——人口增长、农业革命、城市复兴、商业网络、教会改革、十字军、大学诞生、法律复兴、议会起源——各线索并非孤立而是相互嵌套。1300年前后「危机」作为全卷尾声。
background.en: By Jordan (Princeton medievalist, renowned for Capetian France studies). Volume 3, circa 1000–1300. Core thesis: Europe's 'total expansion' of the 11th–13th centuries — population growth, agricultural revolution, urban revival, commercial networks, church reform, crusades, university birth, legal renaissance, parliamentary origins — intertwined rather than isolated. The crises circa 1300 as coda.

plot_acts.zh: c.1000｜从一个公元 1000 年的世界切入——千年前夜的欧洲已蓄势待发。
plot_acts.en: c.1000｜Opens on a world around AD 1000 — Europe on the eve of a thousand-year transformation.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 序章以公元 1000 前夜作为静态切片 —— Jordan 明确拒绝任何单一起点。方法声明：把 1000 当作可以观察的截面而非分水岭。
plot_acts.arg_en: Prologue uses the eve of 1000 as a static cross-section. Method statement: 1000 as observable section, not watershed.

brief.main: 序章 —— 以公元 1000 前夜作为静态切片。Jordan 明确拒绝任何单一起点论 —— 1000 是截面而非分水岭。方法声明：观察这一时点的政治地图、信仰形态、经济水平、社会组织，作为全书三百年变化的起点。
brief.flow: 政治地图 (法兰西王国 / 英格兰七王国之后的威塞克斯统一 / 神圣罗马帝国 / 波兰 Piast / 匈牙利 Árpád / 基辅罗斯 / 拜占庭马其顿王朝 / 伊比利亚的 taifas 分裂) → 教会 (克吕尼改革 910 起、奥托三世的『罗马帝国』理想) → 经济 (三圃制、水力磨坊、城市复兴) → 社会 (封建关系的三阶层叠、军事贵族的世袭化) → 维京-马扎尔-萨拉森三边压力的消退。
brief.names: Otto III、Sylvester II、Robert the Pious、Ethelred II、Bolesław I、Stephen I of Hungary、Vladimir of Kiev、Basil II、Al-Mansur ibn Abi Amir、Hroznata、Bruno of Querfurt
brief.sources: Thietmar of Merseburg、Richer《Historiarum》、Adam of Bremen、Annals of Ulster/Winchester/Quedlinburg、Hildegard (稍后)、Polish Chronicle (Gallus Anonymus, 稍后)
brief.link: 为 Parts I-IV (1000-1300) 铺设静态基线 —— 每一部分都是对这个基线的推动。
brief.main_en: Preface — a static cross-section on the eve of the year 1000. Jordan explicitly rejects any single-origin theory: 1000 is a section, not a watershed. A statement of method — observe the political map, the forms of belief, the level of economy and the social organisation at this instant as the starting point of the book's three centuries of change.
brief.flow_en: The political map (the West Frankish kingdom / the unified Wessex after the Heptarchy / the Holy Roman Empire / Piast Poland / Arpad Hungary / Kievan Rus' / the Macedonian dynasty in Byzantium / the taifa fragmentation of Iberia) → the Church (the Cluniac reform from 910, Otto III's ideal of a 'Roman empire') → the economy (three-field system, watermills, urban revival) → society (the three-orders stratification of feudal relations, the heritarisation of the military nobility) → the ebbing of the three-way Viking-Magyar-Saracen pressure.
brief.names_en: Otto III, Sylvester II, Robert the Pious, Ethelred II, Boleslaw I, Stephen I of Hungary, Vladimir of Kiev, Basil II, al-Mansur ibn Abi Amir, Hroznata, Bruno of Querfurt
brief.sources_en: Thietmar of Merseburg, Richer's Historiae, Adam of Bremen, the Annals of Ulster/Winchester/Quedlinburg, Hildegard (later), the Polish Chronicle (Gallus Anonymus, later)
brief.link_en: Lays a static baseline for Parts I-IV (1000-1300) — each part is a push against this baseline.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第一部 · 11 世纪的欧洲
plot_acts.title_en: PART I · Europe in the Eleventh Century
plot_acts.zh: 1000–1100｜封建奠基、修道院改革、1054 东西教会分裂、诺曼征服、克卢尼运动、十字军前的基督教王国格局。
plot_acts.en: 1000–1100｜Feudal foundations, monastic reform, 1054 schism, Norman conquest, Cluniac movement, pre-crusade Latin Christendom.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第一部分 —— 封建社会的成形 (1000-1100)。卡佩王室、诺曼征服、神圣罗马帝国的萨利安王朝、克吕尼改革 —— 四条并行的政治-宗教线索同步展开。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part I — feudal society 1000-1100. Capetian consolidation, Norman Conquest, Salian HRE, Cluniac reform — four parallel threads.

brief.main: 第一部分 —— 封建欧洲的巩固 (1000-1100)。卡佩王室对法兰西岛的实际掌控、诺曼征服英格兰与西西里、萨利安王朝与教廷的初次冲突、克吕尼改革与格里高利七世的教权宣言 —— 四条并行的政治-宗教线索同步展开。
brief.flow: Ch.1 卡佩王室 (Robert II、Henry I、Philip I) 与法兰西岛的稳固 → Ch.2 诺曼底公国与英格兰征服 (1066) → Ch.3 诺曼人在南意大利与西西里 (Robert Guiscard、Roger I) → Ch.4 萨利安王朝 (Konrad II、Henry III、Henry IV) 与帝国教会制 → Ch.5 克吕尼运动 (Odo、Odilo、Hugh) → 格里高利七世与叙任权之争 (1075-1122) → 第一次十字军 (1095-1099)。
brief.names: Robert II、Henry I of France、Philip I、William the Bastard、Robert Curthose、William II、Henry I of England、Robert Guiscard、Roger I、Bohemond、Conrad II、Henry III、Henry IV、Gregory VII、Clement III、Hugh of Cluny、Odilo、Urban II、Godfrey of Bouillon、Tancred、Raymond of Toulouse、Peter the Hermit
brief.sources: William of Poitiers《Gesta Roberti ducis》、Orderic Vitalis《Historia Ecclesiastica》、Lupus Protospatharius、Annales Normanni、Amalfi 编年史、Domesday Book (1086)、Ivo of Chartres 书信、Gregory VII 教令集、第一十字军三手编年史 (Raymond of Aguilers、Fulcher of Chartres、匿名《Gesta Francorum》)
brief.link: 为第二部分 (12 世纪文艺复兴) 铺设政治-军事框架 —— 没有稳定的封建欧洲，就没有 12 世纪的繁荣。
brief.main_en: Part One — the consolidation of feudal Europe (1000-1100). The Capetians' real grip on the Ile-de-France, the Norman conquests of England and Sicily, the first clash between the Salian dynasty and the papacy, the Cluniac reform and Gregory VII's assertion of papal authority — four parallel political-religious lines unfold together.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 1 the Capetian house (Robert II, Henry I, Philip I) and the securing of the Ile-de-France → ch. 2 the duchy of Normandy and the conquest of England (1066) → ch. 3 the Normans in south Italy and Sicily (Robert Guiscard, Roger I) → ch. 4 the Salian dynasty (Conrad II, Henry III, Henry IV) and the imperial church system → ch. 5 the Cluniac movement (Odo, Odilo, Hugh) → Gregory VII and the Investiture Controversy (1075-1122) → the First Crusade (1095-1099).
brief.names_en: Robert II, Henry I of France, Philip I, William the Bastard, Robert Curthose, William II, Henry I of England, Robert Guiscard, Roger I, Bohemond, Conrad II, Henry III, Henry IV, Gregory VII, Clement III, Hugh of Cluny, Odilo, Urban II, Godfrey of Bouillon, Tancred, Raymond of Toulouse, Peter the Hermit
brief.sources_en: William of Poitiers's Gesta Roberti ducis, Orderic Vitalis's Historia Ecclesiastica, Lupus Protospatharius, the Norman annals, the Amalfi chronicle, Domesday Book (1086), the letters of Ivo of Chartres, the register of Gregory VII, three first-hand chronicles of the First Crusade (Raymond of Aguilers, Fulcher of Chartres, the anonymous Gesta Francorum)
brief.link_en: Lays the political-military framework for Part Two (the twelfth-century renaissance) — without a stable feudal Europe, there is no twelfth-century prosperity.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第二部 · 12 世纪的文艺复兴
plot_acts.title_en: PART II · The Renaissance of the Twelfth Century
plot_acts.zh: 1100–1200｜Chartres 学派、大学肇端、经院哲学萌芽、罗马法复兴、第二十字军、世俗宫廷与抒情诗。
plot_acts.en: 1100–1200｜Chartres school, universities' beginnings, scholasticism, Roman-law revival, Second Crusade, courtly love.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第二部分 —— 12 世纪的文艺复兴。Jordan 沿用 Haskins 但加入社会维度 —— Chartres 学派与大学、罗马法复兴、商业城市兴起被处理为同一进程。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part II — the 12th-century Renaissance. Jordan inherits Haskins but socialises: Chartres, universities, Roman-law revival, commercial cities as one process.

brief.main: 第二部分 —— 12 世纪的文艺复兴。Jordan 沿用 Charles Haskins 的经典命题但加入社会维度 —— Chartres 学派与大学、罗马法复兴、商业城市兴起、王廷文书化被处理为同一进程。方法论最密的一段。
brief.flow: Ch.6 政治版图 (卡佩的 Louis VI、VII、Philip II vs 金雀花 Henry II、Richard I、John；巴巴罗萨与腓特烈一世；科穆宁与拜占庭复兴) → Ch.7 教会与神学 (Bernard、Abelard、Peter Lombard、Hugh of St Victor) → Ch.8 大学的诞生 (Bologna、Paris、Oxford) 与经院方法 → Ch.9 罗马法复兴 (Irnerius、Bologna glossators) 与教令学 (Gratian 1140) → Ch.10 商业革命 (香槟集市、意大利城邦、汉萨前身、货币与信贷) + 12 世纪文艺复兴的艺术 (哥特式、Suger 圣但尼).
brief.names: Louis VI、Louis VII、Eleanor of Aquitaine、Henry II、Eleanor、Richard I、John、Philip II Augustus、Frederick Barbarossa、Henry the Lion、Manuel I Komnenos、Bernard of Clairvaux、Peter Abelard、Heloise、Peter Lombard、Hugh of St Victor、Suger、Abbot Suger、Irnerius、Gratian、Bernard of Chartres、John of Salisbury、Christine de Pizan (稍后)
brief.sources: Suger《De Administratione》、Abelard《Sic et Non》《Historia Calamitatum》、John of Salisbury《Metalogicon》《Policraticus》、Gesta Stephani、Magnus Croner、Chronicon Utinense、Bologna 与 Paris 大学档案、Gratian《Concordia Discordantium Canonum》、罗马法汇编 (Digestum) 的 12 世纪再发现
brief.link: 为第三部分铺路 —— 12 世纪的文化繁荣是 13 世纪教权-王权顶峰的必要条件。
brief.main_en: Part Two — the twelfth-century renaissance. Jordan follows Charles Haskins's classic thesis but adds a social dimension — the School of Chartres and the universities, the revival of Roman law, the rise of the commercial cities and the scribalisation of royal courts are treated as a single process. The most methodologically dense stretch of the book.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 6 the political map (the Capetians Louis VI, VII and Philip II against the Plantagenets Henry II, Richard I and John; Barbarossa and Frederick I; the Komnenoi and the Byzantine revival) → ch. 7 the Church and theology (Bernard, Abelard, Peter Lombard, Hugh of St Victor) → ch. 8 the birth of the university (Bologna, Paris, Oxford) and the scholastic method → ch. 9 the revival of Roman law (Irnerius, the Bolognese glossators) and canon law (Gratian 1140) → ch. 10 the commercial revolution (the fairs of Champagne, the Italian city-states, the precursors of the Hanse, money and credit), plus the art of the twelfth-century renaissance (Gothic, Suger's St-Denis).
brief.names_en: Louis VI, Louis VII, Eleanor of Aquitaine, Henry II, Richard I, John, Philip II Augustus, Frederick Barbarossa, Henry the Lion, Manuel I Komnenos, Bernard of Clairvaux, Peter Abelard, Heloise, Peter Lombard, Hugh of St Victor, Abbot Suger, Irnerius, Gratian, Bernard of Chartres, John of Salisbury, Christine de Pizan (later)
brief.sources_en: Suger's De Administratione, Abelard's Sic et Non and Historia Calamitatum, John of Salisbury's Metalogicon and Policraticus, the Gesta Stephani, the Chronicon Utinense, the archives of the universities of Bologna and Paris, Gratian's Concordia Discordantium Canonum, the twelfth-century rediscovery of the Digest of Roman law
brief.link_en: Paves the way for Part Three — twelfth-century cultural efflorescence is the necessary condition for the thirteenth-century summit of papal and royal power.

plot_acts.zh: 1200–1300｜英诺森三世的教皇君主制、第四次十字军与 1204 君士坦丁堡之陷、阿西西的方济各与多明我、路易九世、托马斯·阿奎那、蒙古西征与欧洲震荡、议会制度成形。
plot_acts.en: 1200–1300｜Innocent III's papal monarchy, Fourth Crusade & 1204, Francis & Dominic, Louis IX, Aquinas, Mongon shock, parliaments.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第三部分 —— 教权-王权的顶峰与冲突 (1200-1300)。英诺森三世的教皇君主制 vs 腓力二世的法国、约翰王与《大宪章》、腓特烈二世的西西里 —— 全书政治密度最高的一段。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part III — apex and conflict of papal-monarchical power (1200-1300). Innocent III vs Philip II, John and Magna Carta, Frederick II's Sicily — the book's densest political stretch.

brief.main: 第三部分 —— 教权-王权的顶峰与冲突 (1200-1300)。全书政治密度最高的一段 —— 英诺森三世的教皇君主制 vs 腓力二世的法国、约翰王与《大宪章》、腓特烈二世的西西里、路易九世的圣王理想。Jordan 处理这一段时最像传统政治史家。
brief.flow: Ch.11 英诺森三世 (1198-1216) 与第四次拉特兰公会议 (1215) → 第四次十字军与君士坦丁堡洗劫 (1204) → 阿尔比十字军 (1209-1229) → Ch.12 腓力二世与布维讷 (1214)、约翰王与《大宪章》(1215)、亨利三世与西门·德·蒙福尔议会 (1265)、路易九世的第七与第八次十字军与皇家司法改革 → Ch.13 腓特烈二世的『世界奇蹟』(Stupor Mundi) 与霍亨斯陶芬王朝的兴衰 (Lucera、Benevento、Tagliacozzo 1266)、Sicilian Vespers (1282).
brief.names: Innocent III、Honorius III、Gregory IX、Innocent IV、Alexander IV、Urban IV、Clement IV、Boniface VIII、Philip II Augustus、John Lackland、Henry III、Simon de Montfort、Louis IX、Margaret of France、Frederick II、Manfred、 Conradin、Charles of Anjou、Michael VIII Palaiologos、Simon de Montfort、Eleanor of Provence、Matthew Paris、Roger Bacon、Thomas Aquinas、Bonaventure
brief.sources: Matthaeus Parisiensis《Historia Anglorum》、Roger of Wendover、Salimbene de Adam《Cronica》、Matthew AIano《Chronicon》、《大宪章》文本、Frederick II《Liber Artis Venandi》、教皇文书 (Regesta)、第四次拉特兰决议、七次十字军的阿拉伯-希腊-拉丁-叙利亚诸记载
brief.link: 为第四部分铺路 —— 13 世纪末的教权崩塌 (Anagni 1303) 直接源于本部分顶峰的反冲。
brief.main_en: Part Three — the summit and conflict of papal and royal power (1200-1300). The most politically dense stretch of the whole book — Innocent III's papal monarchy against Philip II's France, King John and Magna Carta, Frederick II's Sicily, Louis IX's ideal of sainthood. Here Jordan writes most like a conventional political historian.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 11 Innocent III (1198-1216) and the Fourth Lateran Council (1215) → the Fourth Crusade and the sack of Constantinople (1204) → the Albigensian Crusade (1209-1229) → ch. 12 Philip II and Bouvines (1214), King John and Magna Carta (1215), Henry III and Simon de Montfort's parliament (1265), Louis IX's Seventh and Eighth Crusades and royal judicial reform → ch. 13 Frederick II as the 'stupor mundi' and the rise and fall of the Hohenstaufen (Lucera, Benevento, Tagliacozzo 1266), the Sicilian Vespers (1282).
brief.names_en: Innocent III, Honorius III, Gregory IX, Innocent IV, Alexander IV, Urban IV, Clement IV, Boniface VIII, Philip II Augustus, John Lackland, Henry III, Simon de Montfort, Louis IX, Margaret of France, Frederick II, Manfred, Conradin, Charles of Anjou, Michael VIII Palaiologos, Eleanor of Provence, Matthew Paris, Roger Bacon, Thomas Aquinas, Bonaventure
brief.sources_en: Matthew Paris's Historia Anglorum, Roger of Wendover's Flores Historiarum, Salimbene de Adam's Cronica, the text of Magna Carta, Frederick II's De Arte Venandi, the papal regesta, the acts of the Fourth Lateran Council, and the Arabic, Greek, Latin and Syrian accounts of the seven crusades
brief.link_en: Paves the way for Part Four — the collapse of papal power at the end of the thirteenth century (Anagni 1303) stems directly from the recoil against this part's summit.

plot_acts.title_zh: 第四部 · 14 世纪初的基督教世界
plot_acts.title_en: PART IV · Christendom in the Early Fourteenth Century
plot_acts.zh: 1300–1350｜ BONIFACE VIII 与腓力四世的冲突、圣殿骑士团之覆灭、但丁与彼得拉克之间的中世纪晚期张力——黑死病前夜的欧洲。
plot_acts.en: 1300–1350｜Boniface VIII vs Philip IV, Templar suppression, Dante-to-Petrarch tensions — Europe on the eve of the Black Death.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第四部分 —— 信仰社会。Jordan 处理方济各、多明我、贝居因、瓦勒度派 —— 13 世纪不是信仰衰落，而是信仰过剩导致制度无法容纳。
plot_acts.arg_en: Part IV — society of faith. Francis, Dominic, Beguines, Waldensians: 13th c. is faith in excess, institutions cannot contain it.

brief.main: 第四部分 —— 信仰社会。Jordan 处理方济各、多明我、贝居因、瓦勒度派 —— 13 世纪不是信仰衰落，而是信仰过剩导致制度无法容纳。这一部分最像社会-文化史，与 Part III 的政治-外交形成互补。
brief.flow: Ch.14 托钵修会 (方济各 1209、多明我 1216、加尔默罗、奥古斯丁) 与城市布道 → Ch.15 异端 (Cathars、Waldensians、Beguines、Joachimism) 与宗教裁判所 (1233 起) → Ch.16 女性灵修 (Hildegard、Clare of Assisi、Elizabeth of Schönau、Marguerite Porete 1310 火刑) 与宫廷之爱 (troubadours、Marie de France、Chrétien de Troyes、Roman de la Rose)、哥特教堂 (Chartres、Reims、Amiens、Notre-Dame)、经院神学 (Thomas Aquinas、Bonaventure、Duns Scotus、Ockham) 的巅峰。
brief.names: Francis of Assisi、Clare of Assisi、Dominic de Guzmán、Peter Nolasco、Thomas Aquinas、Bonaventure、Duns Scotus、Roger Bacon、Joaquin of Fiore、Peter Waldo、Arnald of Villanova、Marguerite Porete、Meister Eckhart、Hildegard of Bingen、Elizabeth of Schönau、Mechthild of Magdeburg、William IX of Aquitaine、Eleanor of Aquitaine、Marie de France、Chrétien de Troyes、Rutilianus、Wolfram von Eschenbach、Walther von der Vogelweide、Dante (稍后)、Cimabue、Giotto
brief.sources: 方济各会文献 (Bonaventure《Major Life》、Thomas of Celano、早期规则 1221『Regula Prima』)、多明我会 (Jordan of Saxony《Libellus》)、异端审判记录 (Toulouse、Carcassonne、Doles)、贝居因文献 (Marguerite Porete《Mirror of Simple Souls》)、经院神学、编年史、教会会议记录
brief.link: 与 Part III 政治史互补 —— 13 世纪的信仰过剩最终撕裂了政治稳定的可能。
brief.main_en: Part Four — a society of belief. Jordan treats the Franciscans, Dominicans, Beguines and Waldensians: the thirteenth century is not a decline of faith but an excess of faith that institutions cannot contain. This part reads most like social-cultural history, complementing the political-diplomatic Part III.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 14 the mendicant orders (Franciscans 1209, Dominicans 1216, Carmelites, Augustinians) and urban preaching → ch. 15 heresy (Cathars, Waldensians, Beguines, Joachimism) and the Inquisition (from 1233) → ch. 16 women's spirituality (Hildegard, Clare of Assisi, Elizabeth of Schonau, Marguerite Porete burned 1310) and courtly love (troubadours, Marie de France, Chrétien de Troyes, the Roman de la Rose), the Gothic cathedrals (Chartres, Reims, Amiens, Notre-Dame), and the summit of scholastic theology (Thomas Aquinas, Bonaventure, Duns Scotus, Ockham).
brief.names_en: Francis of Assisi, Clare of Assisi, Dominic de Guzman, Peter Nolasco, Thomas Aquinas, Bonaventure, Duns Scotus, Roger Bacon, Joachim of Fiore, Peter Waldo, Arnald of Villanova, Marguerite Porete, Meister Eckhart, Hildegard of Bingen, Elizabeth of Schonau, Mechthild of Magdeburg, William IX of Aquitaine, Eleanor of Aquitaine, Marie de France, Chrétien de Troyes, Wolfram von Eschenbach, Walther von der Vogelweide, Dante (later), Cimabue, Giotto
brief.sources_en: Franciscan texts (Bonaventure's Major Life, Thomas of Celano, the early Regula Prima of 1221), Dominican (Jordan of Saxony's Libellus), heresy trial records (Toulouse, Carcassonne), Beguine texts (Marguerite Porete's Mirror of Simple Souls), scholastic theology, chronicles, acts of church councils
brief.link_en: Complements the political history of Part III — the thirteenth century's excess of faith finally tore apart the possibility of political stability.

plot_acts.zh: c.1350｜从 1000 到 1350——「盛期中世纪」的成就与限度；即将降临的 14 世纪危机。
plot_acts.en: c.1350｜1000 to 1350 — achievements and limits of the High Middle Ages; the fourteenth-century crisis to come.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 尾声 (1300-1350) —— 教权崩塌先于黑死病。Anagni 1303、Avignon 1309、帝国空位期 —— 中世纪晚期的危机不是瘟疫造成，而是瘟疫之前已经内置于结构。这是全书最重要的时序修正。
plot_acts.arg_en: Epilogue 1300-1350: papal collapse precedes Black Death. Anagni, Avignon, imperial interregnum — late-medieval crisis is structural and pre-plague. The book's key chronological correction.

brief.main: 尾声 —— 1300-1350 的崩塌。Jordan 的核心断言：教权崩塌先于黑死病。Anagni 1303、Avignon 1309、帝国空位期 —— 中世纪晚期的危机不是瘟疫造成，而是瘟疫之前已经内置于结构。这是全书最重要的时序修正。
brief.flow: Ch.17 1300 前后 Boniface VIII vs Philip IV (1302 Unam Sanctam、1303 Anagni 事件与 Boniface 之死) → 阿维尼翁之囚 (1309-1377) 与教皇世俗化的开始 → 圣殿骑士团取缔 (1307-1312) → Henry VII 的意大利远征 (1310-1313) 与帝国空位 → 百年战争前夜 (1328 卡佩绝嗣 → Valois 分支) → 大饥荒 1315-1322 → 犹太人与麻风病人迫害 → 1347 黑死病抵达马赛。
brief.names: Boniface VIII、Philip IV、Clement V、John XXII、Benedict XII、Jacques de Molay、Guillaume de Nogaret、Sciarra Colonna、Henry VII、Dante (作为《帝制论》作者)、Louis X、Charles IV、Edward II、Robert the Bruce、Philip VI、Edward III
brief.sources: Vita VIII 的教廷档案、Annales Londonienses、Froissart (稍后)、Ferretus Vinetia《Chronicon》、Dante《帝制论》《神曲》、Marsilius of Padua《Defensor Pacis》(1324)、William of Ockham 政论
brief.link: 直接通向下一卷 —— Jordan 的尾声正是 Vol.4 (若存在) 与任何黑死病后欧洲史的开端。
brief.main_en: Epilogue — the collapse of 1300-1350. Jordan's core claim: the fall of papal power precedes the Black Death. Anagni 1303, Avignon 1309, the imperial interregnum — the crisis of the later Middle Ages is not caused by plague but was built into the structure before the plague arrived. This is the book's most important correction of sequence.
brief.flow_en: Ch. 17 around 1300, Boniface VIII against Philip IV (Unam Sanctam 1302, the Anagni episode and Boniface's death 1303) → the Babylonian Captivity of the papacy (1309-1377) and the beginning of its secularisation → the suppression of the Knights Templar (1307-1312) → Henry VII's Italian expedition (1310-1313) and the imperial interregnum → the eve of the Hundred Years' War (the Capetian extinction 1328, then the Valois branch) → the Great Famine 1315-1322 → the persecution of Jews and lepers → the Black Death reaching Marseille in 1347.
brief.names_en: Boniface VIII, Philip IV, Clement V, John XXII, Benedict XII, Jacques de Molay, Guillaume de Nogaret, Sciarra Colonna, Henry VII, Dante (as author of De Monarchia), Louis X, Charles IV, Edward II, Robert the Bruce, Philip VI, Edward III
brief.sources_en: The papal archives on the life of Boniface VIII, the Annales Londonienses, Froissart (later), Ferretto of Verona's Chronicon, Dante's De Monarchia and Commedia, Marsilius of Padua's Defensor Pacis (1324), the political writings of William of Ockham
brief.link_en: Leads directly to the next volume — Jordan's epilogue is precisely the opening of the post-plague history of Europe.

narrative.zh: 以「扩张」为核心概念的统一论：领土扩张（东进、十字军）、经济扩张（垦殖、城市化、贸易）、知识扩张（大学、翻译）、制度扩张（教会法、普通法、议会）——四条线编织在一起，在约1300汇聚为「危机」。
narrative.en: Unified by 'expansion' as core concept: territorial (eastward, crusades), economic (reclamation, urbanization, trade), intellectual (universities, translation), institutional (canon law, common law, parliament) — four threads braided together, converging into 'crisis' circa 1300.

characters.name: Pope Innocent III · 教皇英诺森三世
characters.role_zh: 1160–1216，中世纪教权的顶峰——第四次拉特兰公会议召集者
characters.role_en: Papal monarchy — 1160–1216, the summit of medieval papal authority; convener of the Fourth Lateran Council

characters.name: Francis of Assisi · 阿西西的方济各
characters.role_zh: 1181–1226，贫困运动与世俗教会的张力
characters.role_en: Mendicant orders — 1181–1226, the tension between the poverty movement and the secular church

characters.name: Louis IX of France · 法兰西的路易九世
characters.role_zh: 1214–1270，圣路易——第七与第八次十字军与皇家司法改革
characters.role_en: Capetian France — 1214–1270, Saint Louis; the Seventh and Eighth Crusades and royal judicial reform

characters.name: Thomas Aquinas · 托马斯·阿奎那
characters.role_zh: 1225–1274，《神学大全》——亚里士多德革命与基督教综合
characters.role_en: Scholasticism — 1225–1274, the Summa Theologiae; the Aristotelian revolution and the Christian synthesis

characters.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine · 阿基坦的埃莉诺
characters.role_zh: 1122–1204，两位王后与十字军随行——12 世纪女性权力的极点
characters.role_en: Poitou-France-England — 1122–1204, queen twice over and a crusade companion; the peak of twelfth-century women's power

quotes.orig: The central bond tying man to man in rural society was the personal tie of loyalty.
quotes.trans_zh: 乡村社会中维系人与人的核心纽带，是忠诚这一私人关系。
quotes.source: Jordan《中世纪盛期的欧洲》· 正文 · 社会结构
quotes.source_en: William Chester Jordan, Europe in the High Middle Ages · Social Structure

quotes.orig: One of the most striking features of southern life in eleventh-century Europe was the presence of a strong urban culture, not entirely discontinuous with the ancient past.
quotes.trans_zh: 十一世纪欧洲南部生活最引人注目的特征之一，是一种强健的城市文化的存在——它与古代过去并非全然断裂。
quotes.source: Jordan《中世纪盛期的欧洲》· 正文 · 地中海世界
quotes.source_en: William Chester Jordan, Europe in the High Middle Ages · The Mediterranean World

intent.reception_good_zh: 叙事清晰、结构优雅——被广泛用作欧美大学中世纪史课程教材。
intent.reception_good_en: Clear narrative, elegant structure — widely adopted for undergraduate medieval-history courses.
intent.reception_bad_zh: 结构性保留有二：受制于教科书式篇幅，东欧、拜占庭与伊比利亚再征服被压缩，叙事重心仍是法兰西—英格兰—德意志的核心西欧；方法上偏重政治、宗教与制度的传统叙事，对社会—经济史、性别与边缘群体的新近研究吸收有限，故被一些学者视为稳健却略趋保守。作为断代合成，它对十二至十三世纪「危机」与「转折」的因果裁断有时让位于清晰时间线。
intent.reception_bad_en: Two structural reservations: bound by textbook length, the Eastern periphery, Byzantium and the Iberian Reconquista get squeezed, with the narrative anchored on France-England-Germany; and the method stays close to conventional political, religious and institutional narrative, absorbing less of the newer social-economic, gender and subaltern scholarship, so some read it as sound but slightly conservative. As a period synthesis its causal verdicts on the crises of the twelfth-thirteenth centuries can yield to a clean timeline.
intent.syn_zh: 「扩张」是理解中世纪盛期欧洲的唯一关键词——直到扩张本身成为危机。
intent.syn_en: 'Expansion' is the single keyword for High Medieval Europe — until expansion itself became crisis.

craft.zh: 以单一概念（expansion）统一多线叙事的写作策略
craft.en: Unifying multi-thread narrative under a single concept (expansion)

craft.zh: Jordan 的清楚胜于博学 —— 本书是英语世界最好的中世纪大学教科书之一。
craft.en: Clarity over erudition — among the finest English medieval textbooks.

craft.zh: 按 4 部分时间推进，每部分内按政-社-经-宗-文分专题 —— 结构与叙述的复合。
craft.en: 4-part chronological spine, each with thematic sub-sections inside.

craft.zh: 大量使用一手编年史的直接引用 —— 让中世纪人自己说话。
craft.en: Heavy direct quotation of medieval chroniclers.

craft.zh: 内外联动的「扩张」概念：把内部殖民（垦荒、排水、排犹与驱逐异端）与外部地中海/十字军扩张并置为同一逻辑的两面，使单一关键词获得结构性而非装饰性的解释力。
craft.en: Expansion as an inner-outer coupling: internal colonisation (land clearance, drainage, expulsion of Jews and heretics) is set beside Mediterranean and crusading expansion as two faces of one logic, giving the single keyword structural rather than decorative explanatory force.

motifs.evid_zh: 从克吕尼到方济各，宗教改革不是 16 世纪独有——中世纪自有其内部革命。
motifs.evid_en: From Cluny to Francis, religious reform is not exclusive to the 16th century — the Middle Ages had its own inner revolutions.

motifs.evid_zh: 英诺森三世达到顶峰——本书最重要的政治制度史线索。
motifs.evid_en: Reaching its summit under Innocent III — the book's most important line of political-institutional history.

motifs.evid_zh: 博洛尼亚、巴黎、牛津——知识的制度化在 12-13 世纪成型。
motifs.evid_en: Bologna, Paris, Oxford — the institutionalisation of knowledge takes shape in the 12th-13th centuries.

motifs.evid_zh: 从 1095 到 1291，拉丁基督教与拜占庭-伊斯兰的三角。
motifs.evid_en: From 1095 to 1291, the triangle of Latin Christendom, Byzantium and Islam.

excerpts.orig: The forty-seven-year-old Alsatian pilgrim, Bruno of Egisheim, who made his way more than 600 miles from Worms to Rome in 1049, had only recently become Pope Leo IX. In the cortege with this future saint, canonized in 1087, was a group of earnest and purposeful companions, including Abbot Hugh of Cluny and a still little-known Tuscan monk by the name of Hildebrand. These men and a few others like them had a conception of the universal Church and of a universal Christian society (Christendom) that they would impose imperfectly but in grimly determined stages and with enormous consequences on the princes and bishops of the Catholic faithful. In the person of the new pope, the conception was revealed principally through his unceasing efforts to eradicate simony, the purchase of ecclesiastical offices, a practice that placed local churches under the control of influential families and, thereby, permitted aristocrats of the period to exploit and impoverish local churches or to use them as pawns in their feuds.
excerpts.trans_zh: 公元 1000 年前夜的欧洲，已经在物质、政治与宗教层面蓄势待发。
excerpts.note_zh: 以千年前夜切入——盛期中世纪不是一场突变，而是三个世纪的缓慢成熟。
excerpts.note_en: Opens on the eve of the first millennium — the High Middle Ages matured, not erupted.

excerpts.orig: Its polemical resonance now considerably softened, the phrase ‘Renaissance of the twelfth century’ – if we accept the breadth of the dating favoured by Haskins, acknowledge the new as well as the renewed in the period, and factor in reforms in religious life and vernacular culture – is an apt description of the era we shall now be exploring.
excerpts.trans_zh: 十二世纪的「文艺复兴」—— Chartres 学派、大学、罗马法复兴、经院哲学与抒情诗共同构成一场文化的自发性爆发。
excerpts.note_zh: 「12 世纪文艺复兴」——Jordan 沿用了 Haskins 的经典命题并加入社会维度。
excerpts.note_en: The 12th-century Renaissance: Chartres, universities, Roman-law revival, scholasticism, lyric poetry.

excerpts.orig: To compensate for these new demands – when they did not simply refuse to pay them – peasants were forced into debt. With so little in disposable funds, they cut corners on their farms and took the worst kinds of chances against good sense, trying, for example, to bring land under cultivation that was marginal at best. They resorted to poaching and other forms of theft. But still the burden of their debt mounted, without any noticeable reduction in pressure on them from the upper classes to fulfil their fiscal obligations. The countryside, and again one is speaking of the West, became a powder keg. The alternatives were either submission to a new enserfment, perhaps on the degrading mode of eastern Europe, or peasant rebellion.
excerpts.trans_zh: 十四世纪初的基督教世界已在内部撕裂——Boniface VIII 与腓力四世的冲突是教皇君主制的丧钟。
excerpts.note_zh: 以 1300-1350 的教权崩塌收尾——黑死病之前的信仰世界已自身动摇。
excerpts.note_en: Ends with the collapse of papal monarchy 1300-1350 — faith was already fractured before the Black Death.

fact_ledger.claim: Viking 2001, 464pp, ISBN 9780140285700 (Penguin pb)
William Chester Jordan = Princeton, Dayton-Stockton Prof. of History

read_through.verdict_zh: Jordan 盛期中世纪 1000-1300 的实质是一部『三场内生革命 + 一场崩塌』：教会改革 (克吕尼→格里高利七世→英诺森三世)、政治封建化 (卡佩-金雀花-神圣罗马帝国-诺曼英格兰的相互塑造)、文化与经济 (12 世纪文艺复兴、大学、商业革命)，然后从 1300 起进入黑死病前夜的教权-王权同时崩塌。通读全书最印象深刻的是 Jordan 对『信仰社会』的处理——中世纪晚期不是信仰衰微，而是信仰的过剩导致的内部撕裂。第 III 部分（教会与政治）是全书最完整的一块，也是英语世界最好的中世纪教科书之一。
read_through.verdict_en: Jordan's 1000-1300 is really three internal revolutions plus one collapse: church reform (Cluny → Gregory VII → Innocent III), political feudalisation (Capetian-Plantagenet-HRE-Norman England mutual shaping), cultural-economic (12th-c. Renaissance, universities, commercial revolution) — then from 1300 the simultaneous breakdown of papal and royal authority before the Black Death. Most memorable on a full read is Jordan on 'society of faith': the late Middle Ages were not declining faith but faith's excess tearing itself. Part III (Church and Politics) is the book's most complete block and among the finest medieval textbooks in English.

observations.title_zh: Prologue 的方法声明
observations.note_zh: 以『公元 1000 前夜』的静态画面开篇，Jordan 明确拒绝任何单一起点论——他把 1000 当作一个可以观察的横截面而非分水岭。这个立场贯穿全书，也解释了他为什么没有把 1066 或 1095 作为分章依据。
observations.note_en: Opens on 1000 as a cross-section, not a watershed — hence no reliance on 1066 or 1095 as chapter breaks; the whole book inherits this static-slice method.

observations.title_zh: PART II 的『12 世纪文艺复兴』处理
observations.note_zh: Jordan 沿用 Charles Haskins 的经典命题但加入社会维度 —— Chartres 学派与大学不是孤立的智识事件，而是与商业城市兴起、罗马法复兴、王廷文书化同步发生。这一节是全书方法论最密之处。
observations.note_en: Jordan inherits Haskins but socialises it: Chartres and universities rise with commercial cities, Roman-law revival, chancery writing — the densest methodological passage in the book.

observations.title_zh: PART IV 的教权崩塌先于黑死病
observations.note_zh: 第 IV 部分（1300-1350）的核心断言：Boniface VIII vs Philip IV (1303 Anagni)、Avignon Captivity (1309)、Holy Roman Empire 空位期——教会君主制的合法性在瘟疫之前已经动摇。这是本书最重要的时序修正。
observations.note_en: Part IV (1300-1350): Anagni 1303, Avignon 1309, imperial interregnum — papal monarchy's legitimacy was already compromised before the plague. The book's most important chronological correction.

observations.title_zh: 对女性权力的克制处理
observations.note_zh: Jordan 对 Eleanor of Aquitaine、Hildegard of Bingen、Christine de Pizan 的处理都是结构性而非传奇性——他不把她们写成例外，而是写成封建-修道-宫廷三条通道下的可能位置。这在 2001 年出版的教科书里是罕见的克制。
observations.note_en: Eleanor, Hildegard, Christine handled structurally rather than as wonders — as possible positions under feudal / monastic / court channels. Unusually restrained for a 2001 textbook.

full_analysis.zh: **通读后的整体判断**：Jordan 本书是英语世界最好的中世纪教科书之一 —— 这个『最好』的核心是它的**克制**。作者既不把 1000-1300 写成进步叙事 (Pirenne 传统的商业化叙述)，也不写成衰亡前夜 (Huizinga 的 Autumn 传统)，而是把这三百年作为『一个刚刚成形的信仰-政治社会在其内部张力下同时达到顶峰与解体前夜』。方法上：Jordan 大量直接引用一手编年史 (Orderic Vitalis, Joinville, Matthew Paris, Jean de Joinville, Froissart) —— 让中世纪人自己说话，是本书在同类教科书里最坚持的一条。局限：(1) 对 11-13 世纪的商业革命处理过简 —— 与 Pirenne/Henri Pirenne 后续研究 (Abulafia, Lopez, Epstein) 相比明显收缩；(2) 对犹太人与穆斯林在盛期中世纪的位置只在第 IV 部分末尾各一节 —— 与今天中世纪史学界 (David Nirenberg, Jeremy Cohen) 的讨论相比滞后；(3) 十字军的处理偏政治-军事，缺少 Jonathan Riley-Smith / Thomas Asbridge 一代的内部社会史维度。
full_analysis.en: **Overall verdict after a full read**: Jordan's is among the finest English-language medieval textbooks — and 'finest' here means restraint. Neither progress narrative (Pirenne commercialisation) nor dusk-of-the-middle-ages (Huizinga), Jordan treats 1000-1300 as a just-formed faith-polity reaching apex and eve of dissolution simultaneously. Methodologically heavy direct quotation of chroniclers (Orderic, Joinville, Matthew Paris, Froissart) — letting medieval people speak. Limitations: (1) commercial revolution under-covered relative to Pirenne's successors (Abulafia, Lopez, Epstein); (2) Jews and Muslims only get sub-sections at end of Part IV, lagging Nirenberg/Cohen's current scholarship; (3) Crusades treated politically-militarily, missing Riley-Smith / Asbridge's internal social-history dimension.

books.why_zh: 从路德贴出九十五条到威斯特伐利亚和约——一百三十年的宗教战争如何彻底摧毁了中世纪基督教世界的统一？Greengrass 给出最完整的政治-文化合成叙事。
books.why_en: From Luther's 95 Theses to Westphalia — how did 130 years of religious wars destroy medieval Christendom's unity? Greengrass delivers the fullest political-cultural synthesis.

background.zh: Greengrass（谢菲尔德大学近代早期史荣休教授，前格拉斯哥、Warwick）撰写第五卷。时间跨度 1517–1648：从路德发难到三十年战争结束的威斯特伐利亚和约。核心论题：「基督教世界」(Christendom) 不是一个制度而是一种共同想象——宗教改革打破了这个想象，而打破后的代价是一百三十年的内战与外交重组。涵盖瑞士改革、再洗礼派、法国宗教战争、尼德兰革命、西班牙黄金时代、古斯塔夫二世、三十年战争。Greengrass 另一部成名作是《The European Reformation, c.1450–1618》（1996 初版，2015 第 3 版），是英语宗教改革史的标准教科书。
background.en: By Greengrass (Emeritus Prof of Early Modern History, University of Sheffield; previously Glasgow and Warwick). Volume 5, 1517–1648: from Luther to Westphalia. Core thesis: 'Christendom' was not an institution but a shared imagination — the Reformation broke it, and the price of breaking it was 130 years of civil war and diplomatic reorganization. Covers Swiss Reformation, Anabaptists, French Wars of Religion, Dutch Revolt, Spanish Golden Age, Gustavus Adolphus, Thirty Years' War. His companion book The European Reformation (1996, 3rd ed. 2015) is the English-language textbook.

plot_acts.zh: 1517–1648｜路德 95 条的钉子作为开场——本书论「基督教世界 (Christendom)」如何作为一个共同想象被拆开。
plot_acts.en: 1517–1648｜Luther's theses as prologue — this is the story of how 'Christendom' as a shared imagination was broken.

plot_acts.arg_zh: Introduction —— 定题：『基督教世界』作为可拆分的共同想象。全书方法论声明，之后每一节都在这条线上工作。
plot_acts.arg_en: Introduction: Christendom as a divisible shared imagination. Method statement; every subsequent section works on this line.

brief.main: 定题 —— 『基督教世界』(Christendom) 从『制度』重新定义为『共同想象』。全书方法论声明：1517 之前的欧洲不是政治统一，而是可被共同想象维系的信仰-文化共同体。之后每一节都在这条线上工作 —— 展示这个想象如何在神学、政治、艺术、印刷、朝圣五条边界上被同时拆散。
brief.flow: 1500 前夜的基督教世界地图 (拉丁西方 vs 东正教东欧-俄罗斯、奥斯曼巴尔干-安纳托利亚) → 教廷的世俗化 (Borgia、Renaissance papacy) → 人文主义 (Erasmus、More、Reuchlin、Clichtthovius) → 印刷术 (1450 谷登堡 → 1500 已印 2000 万册) → 城市与商业网络 (Fugger、Welser) → 朝圣与圣物经济 → 与拜占庭的对照 (1453 陷落的余波) → 提出本书的溶解论。
brief.names: Alexander VI、Julius II、Leo X、Erasmus、Thomas More、Reuchlin、Trithemius、Sforza、Medici、Fugger、Gutenberg、Aldus Manutius、Savonarola
brief.sources: Erasmus《Praise of Folly》(1511)、《Epistolae Obscurorum Virorum》(1515)、Solinus《De Situ Orbis》、1500 年禧年记录、Aldine 版本、Fugger 家族账簿、Sforza-Medici 通信
brief.link: 为全书定题 —— 之后每一节都在证明这个『共同想象』如何被拆散。
brief.main_en: Framing — 'Christendom' is redefined from an institution into a shared imagination. The book's methodological statement: Europe before 1517 was not politically unified but a faith-culture community held together by a common imagination. Every later section works along this line — showing how that imagination was simultaneously pulled apart along five boundaries: theology, politics, art, print, and pilgrimage.
brief.flow_en: The map of Christendom on the eve of 1500 (Latin West vs Orthodox Eastern Europe-Russia, Ottoman Balkans-Anatolia) → the secularisation of the papacy (Borgia, the Renaissance papacy) → humanism (Erasmus, More, Reuchlin, Clichthovius) → printing (Gutenberg 1450 → some 20 million printed volumes by 1500) → cities and commercial networks (Fugger, Welser) → the pilgrimage-and-relic economy → the contrast with Byzantium (the aftermath of the 1453 fall) → the statement of the book's dissolution thesis.
brief.names_en: Alexander VI, Julius II, Leo X, Erasmus, Thomas More, Reuchlin, Trithemius, Sforza, Medici, Fugger, Gutenberg, Aldus Manutius, Savonarola
brief.sources_en: Erasmus's Praise of Folly (1511), the Epistolae Obscurorum Virorum (1515), Solinus's De Situ Orbis, the 1500 jubilee records, the Aldine editions, the Fugger family ledgers, the Sforza-Medici correspondence
brief.link_en: Frames the whole book — every later section proves how this 'shared imagination' was taken apart.

plot_acts.en: 1450–1600｜Papal authority, Ottoman pressure, print, discovery, theological rupture — the end of 'one Western church'.
plot_acts.sources: EPUB TOC extracted from original book
plot_acts.arg_zh: 第一节 —— 1500 年前夜欧洲的宗教-文化状态。Greengrass 拒绝把中世纪晚期写成『腐化的教会等着被改革』，而是呈现一个多元、活力、但也充满张力的信仰世界。
plot_acts.arg_en: Section 1 — religious-cultural Europe on the eve of 1500. Refuses the 'corrupt church awaiting reform' teleology; presents a plural, vigorous, tension-filled faith-world.

brief.main: 路德与宗教改革的爆发 —— 95 条 (1517.10.31) 到奥格斯堡和约 (1555)。Greengrass 处理这一段时强调：路德之所以能被保护，不是因为神学，而是因为萨克森选帝侯 Frederick the Wise 与帝国政治的缝隙。一个皇帝的失败作为整个天主教世界解体的第一块多米诺。
brief.flow: 路德维滕贝格 95 条 → 莱比锡辩论 (1519) → 教皇训令 (1520) 焚毁 → Worms 议会 (1521) 与 Wartburg 隐居 → 茨维考先知与农民战争 (1524-1525，闵采尔) → 施马卡登联盟 (1531) → 奥格斯堡 Confessio (1530) → 查理五世的奥格斯堡和约 (1555) 与 cuius regio eius religio。
brief.names: Martin Luther、Frederick the Wise、Charles V、Carlstadt、Zwingli、Melanchthon、Landgrave Philip of Hesse、Thomas Müntzer、Duke George of Saxony、Eck、Tetzel、Leo X、Adrian VI、Clement VII
brief.sources: 路德《95 条》《教会被掳于巴比伦》《论善功》《大/小教理问答》《桌边谈》、Melanchthon《Loci Communes》《奥格斯堡 Confessio》、Zwingli 苏黎世辩论记录、农民战争十二条款、Müntzer 书信、Worms 议会记录、Catechism 诸版
brief.link: 为第二节 (加尔文与多元改革) 铺路 —— 路德只是多元改革的第一种可能。
brief.main_en: Luther and the outbreak of the Reformation — from the 95 Theses (31 Oct 1517) to the Peace of Augsburg (1555). Handling this passage Greengrass stresses that Luther was protected not because of theology but because of the gap between Frederick the Wise, elector of Saxony, and Imperial politics. One emperor's failure as the first domino of the whole Catholic world's dissolution.
brief.flow_en: Luther's 95 Theses at Wittenberg → the Leipzig Debate (1519) → the papal bull burned (1520) → the Diet of Worms (1521) and the Wartburg hiding → the Zwickau prophets and the Peasants' War (1524-1525, Müntzer) → the Schmalkaldic League (1531) → the Augsburg Confession (1530) → Charles V's Peace of Augsburg (1555) and cuius regio eius religio.
brief.names_en: Martin Luther, Frederick the Wise, Charles V, Carlstadt, Zwingli, Melanchthon, Landgrave Philip of Hesse, Thomas Müntzer, Duke George of Saxony, Eck, Tetzel, Leo X, Adrian VI, Clement VII
brief.sources_en: Luther's 95 Theses, On the Babylonian Captivity of the Church, Treatise on Good Works, the Large and Small Catechisms, the Table Talk; Melanchthon's Loci Communes and the Augsburg Confession; the records of the Zurich Disputations; the Twelve Articles of the Peasants; Müntzer's letters; the Diet of Worms records; the various Catechism editions
brief.link_en: Paves the way for the second section (Calvin and the plural reforms) — Luther is only the first possibility of a plural Reformation.
